overview: A one-page Department of State list of papers, dated November 30, 1945, for a file concerning the territorial status of Formosa (Taiwan). It records a single April 1, 1939 communication from Taihoku associated with Warner, concerning the extension of the Taiwan Government-General’s jurisdiction over the Shinnan Gunto, a group of islands in the South China Sea now generally identified with the Spratly Islands.

people.name: Gerald Warner
people.role: U.S. diplomatic or consular officer associated with the April 1, 1939 communication from Taihoku

subfiles.title: Department of State list of papers on Formosa and the Shinnan Gunto
subfiles.about: This filing sheet inventories a 1939 communication concerning the Taiwan Government-General’s jurisdiction over the Shinnan Gunto in the South China Sea.
subfiles.summary: The sheet identifies the file subject as “Territory - Formosa, Taiwan.” Its sole entry describes an April 1, 1939 communication from Taihoku associated with Warner. According to the summary, jurisdiction over the Shinnan Gunto—a group of South China Sea islands—had been assigned to the Taiwan Government-General, and the underlying communication supplied information about the islands.

interest: Although the underlying 1939 communication is not present, this filing sheet preserves evidence that the State Department tracked Japan’s administrative incorporation of the Shinnan Gunto under the Taiwan Government-General. It is useful for tracing prewar documentation of the Spratly Islands dispute and for identifying a potentially important missing or separately filed diplomatic report. The 1945 compilation date also places the retrospective cataloguing at the moment when Japanese rule over Taiwan and its wartime island claims was ending.
